references.text: God hardened Pharaoh's heart, a similar theme where the Lord hardens a ruler's heart to fulfill His plan.
The Lord says He will harden Pharaoh's heart, the same pattern as with Sihon, where God hardens a king's heart.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart so he would not listen to Moses, parallel to how Sihon's spirit was hardened.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, a recurring theme of divine hardening of rulers.
The Lord hardened their hearts so they went to war against Israel, the same pattern where God hardens enemies to deliver them up.
Sihon refused to let Israel pass through his land and gathered his army, the historical account this verse refers to.
Reference to the victory over Sihon, king of Heshbon, and how God gave him into Israel's hand.
God commands to make the people's hearts hard, the same theme of divine hardening to fulfill His purpose.
Paul discusses how God hardens whom He wills, with reference to Pharaoh, the same theological principle.
